# Plan to double Sunday Crust subscribers in 30 days

Doubling from 140 to 280 in 30 days means about 35 new subscribers a week. That's possible, but only if the plan is built around referrals and the Christmas season, not paid ads. €300 a month in ads won't get you 140 people. Your existing customers and the shop counter can.

## First, check capacity (days 1–3)
Before chasing growth, make sure you can handle 280 boxes on a Saturday morning:
- **Baking:** Can 3 people bake twice the volume Friday night into Saturday? If not, cap the push at what you can bake, or bring in one part-time baker or rider for Saturdays.
- **Delivery:** How many boxes fit in one cargo bike trip, and how many trips fit in the morning? Plan routes by area now. Consider adding a **pickup option at the shop** for €2 off. It takes pressure off delivery and reaches people beyond the 3 km radius.
- If you're short on capacity, open a **waitlist** rather than letting delivery quality slip. Losing early subscribers to late or damaged boxes would cancel out the growth.

## The four levers, ranked by expected impact

**1. Referral programme (target: 50–60 new)**
- Offer "Give a box, get a box": the friend gets their first box free and the referrer gets a free box once the friend pays for a second week.
- Put a printed card with a personal code in every box for the next 4 Saturdays, and send an email or WhatsApp message to all 140 subscribers.
- Each free box costs you the ingredients and time, not €18. That's cheaper than any ad, and referred subscribers usually stay longer.
- For a 40% response rate, make it easy: one link and a ready-made message they can forward.

**2. Christmas gift subscriptions (target: 30–40 new)**
- This is the biggest opportunity right now. Sell 4-week and 8-week gift boxes (€72 and €144) with a nice printed card, delivered from the first or second Saturday in December.
- Promote them at the counter, in every box and on Instagram. Sell them to local companies as client or staff gifts.
- When a gift ends, ask the recipient to continue. That's where gift buyers become regular subscribers.

**3. Convert people already buying from you (target: 25–35 new)**
- Your walk-in customers already like your bread. Train the team to make one pitch at the till: "Want this delivered every Saturday? First box is half price."
- Put a sign and a QR code at the till, plus a sign-up sheet.
- Hand out free tasting slices on the busiest days.

**4. Local saturation within 3 km (target: 20–30 new)**
- Spend most of the €300 on flyers with a half-price first box offer, dropped on the streets where you already deliver. Cargo bike routes are most efficient when density goes up.
- Post in neighbourhood Facebook and WhatsApp groups and on Nextdoor-style platforms, with a photo of a real Saturday box.
- Partner with 2–3 places that don't sell bread, like a coffee shop, a co-working space, a gym or a cheese shop. Leave a stack of cards with them and give them a free box.
- Offer workplace subscriptions. One delivery stop with 8 boxes is very efficient.
- Pitch the local paper or a city blog: "Bakery delivers bread by cargo bike." Media likes that story, especially in winter.

## Week by week
| Week | Focus |
|---|---|
| 1 | Check capacity, set up the pickup option, print referral cards and gift cards, brief the team, email subscribers |
| 2 | Launch referrals in every box, start the till pitch, drop flyers on half the area, post in local groups |
| 3 | Push gift subscriptions hard, contact companies, set up partner cards, send the press pitch, drop the second flyer wave |
| 4 | Last call for Christmas gifts, send a referral reminder, phone or message everyone who took a trial box to convert them |

## Watch these numbers weekly
- New sign-ups by source. Use a different code per channel so you know what works.
- Trial-to-paid conversion. Free or half-price first boxes only count if people stay. Aim for over 50%.
- Cancellations. Doubling doesn't help if 30 existing subscribers leave over Christmas, so consider a "pause for holidays" option instead of cancelling.

## My honest view
Realistically, I'd expect **+80 to +140**. Hitting 280 depends mostly on how many of your 140 subscribers refer someone and how well the Christmas gifts sell. Even +80 in a month would be a very strong result for a three-person bakery.

To sharpen the plan, it would help to know three things: your margin per box, your current Saturday capacity, and your monthly cancellation rate. Your margin decides how generous the referral offer can be.
